tools.name: deploy_folder
tools.description:
Deploy web assets or a fullstack project using EdgeOne CLI. workspacePath is the local project root, NOT a cloud workspace. Existing .edgeone/project.json is authoritative: ordinary deployment follows its project/workspace, even after global workspace switching. Do not change projectName to bypass a link or auth error. For a new project, confirm its meaningful name and target before creating it.
If status is selection_required, deployment has NOT started: ask the user to choose an available workspace (never choose the first), then call edgeone_workspace with action=login, the exact workspaceId/sessionId and returned workspacePath; after completed authentication retry this original deployment. Show waiting browser links to the user. If status is workspace_confirmation_required, connector login is already complete: obtain choices via edgeone_workspace action=use without workspaceId, ask the user neutrally, select their exact ID and retry; do not use the automatically selected workspace as a recommendation or start login again. If status is authentication_required, explain the linked workspace credential requirement, obtain consent for switching global credentials, then call edgeone_workspace action=use with the returned workspaceId; complete login and retry. A workspace switch does not authorize re-linking or migration. Never invent CLI workspace flags, read cached tokens, or silently modify credential sources. Preserve the returned deployment URL exactly, including its query string. On errors, report the cause rather than silently deploying elsewhere.
Customer-facing communication: Keep messages friendly, concise and focused on the next action or actual outcome, in the user's language. Keep sessionId, workspaceId, ZoneId, status codes, CLI commands and resume/reconnect mechanics internal; do not repeat raw tool JSON or technical logs to the customer. In Chinese avoid terms such as 会话、登录恢复、凭证绑定; say 登录、选择工作空间、继续部署 instead. Only explain implementation details if explicitly asked.
Present workspace names neutrally using the host's selection control. Do not recommend, rank, preselect or label a workspace as preferred, and do not infer a choice from its order, name or plan. Add only the minimum non-sensitive label needed to distinguish duplicate names; show plan/status only when requested or needed to explain unavailability. Do not hide choices because of host option limits; page them if needed. Keep exact IDs internal for tool calls. Do not offer unavailable workspaces as selectable.
Examples for deployment: before browser authentication, 请打开链接完成登录。; when a choice is needed, 请选一个工作空间用于这次部署。; after completed authentication, continue the original task without asking the customer to say continue or showing intermediate commands. Report 正在部署，请稍候。 only while deployment is actually running; report 部署成功： followed by the exact returned URL only after success. Skip unnecessary intermediate messages and repeated login prompts. Use wording appropriate to the original task; never imply a deployment is happening during a read-only query.
For project-link failures, use the returned errorCode and message instead of guessing: PROJECT_ALREADY_EXISTS means duplicate creation was refused, PROJECT_NOT_FOUND means the target was not found, PROJECT_LOOKUP_FAILED means the query failed, and LINK_CANCELLED means actual cancellation. Generic legacy CLI errors do not prove user cancellation, a hidden confirmation dialog or a name conflict. Verify the intended workspace/project before offering a user-approved existing-project link or another name; never automatically rename, change modes or retry creation. Tell the customer the specific cause briefly, not a list of speculative possibilities.
Translate technical errors into a brief actionable explanation without hiding their cause or claiming success. A genuinely expired login can be explained as 登录等待时间已过，请重新打开链接完成登录。 Do not describe a missing in-memory record as expiry or ask for a new login solely because the connection changed. Continue to obtain consent before changing login sources or project targets; use plain language such as 这个项目属于工作空间「名称」，需要登录后才能继续。

builtFolderPath.description: Provide the absolute path to the folder containing deployable web assets (HTML, CSS, JS, images, etc.). This can be either a build output directory (like dist/, build/, out/) or a folder with static files ready for deployment.

workspacePath.description: Absolute local project directory, not a cloud workspace ID.

projectName.description: Meaningful name for a NEW project. Use letters, digits, underscores or hyphens, starting with a letter or digit. Omit for an existing directory link; never use renaming to bypass workspace mismatches.

workspaceId.description: Optional expected cloud Workspace ID; verifies the target, does not switch or re-link the directory.

projectType.description: Specify the project type. Choose 'fullstack' for NextJS full-stack projects, or 'static' for static sites and other build tool outputs. Note: If workspacePath contains any of the directories 'functions', 'node-functions', or 'edge-functions', it should be considered a fullstack project.

tools.name: edgeone_workspace
tools.description:
Use this tool first whenever the user wants to list or switch workspaces; do not look up CLI commands or scan credentials. Default scope=global: list is read-only; use changes global credentials only and preserves the directory project; login starts or resumes authentication. To deploy this existing page in another workspace, use action=use with scope=project after explicit user consent: read account_info for the previous linkedProject.ProjectId, confirm the target workspace/name and mode (link_existing or separately authorized create_upload), then provide workspaceId, projectName, mode, confirmed=true and expectedProjectId. This call authenticates the chosen workspace and then changes the original directory association using the same safe linking flow as edgeone_project_link. Do not copy to a new directory or manually edit/delete project.json to bypass a link. Local environment files are preserved; original cloud projects/data are not migrated or deleted, and this tool does not deploy. Only after verified success continue deploy_folder against the same directory, omitting replacement names.
With action=use and an exact chosen workspaceId, cached credentials are reused; if missing, this tool starts Agent browser login and emits waiting links. Keep it running and display the login link rather than sending the user to a terminal. For initial neutral workspace choices omit workspaceId with scope=global, then submit the explicitly chosen target. On selection_required never select the first candidate. If a project-scope response includes continuation, reuse it with the exact user-selected available ID and returned sessionId in the same directory; preserve scope and project-confirmation fields, including after MCP reconnect/restart. Without project scope, resume action=login with the original sessionId and chosen workspaceId. Sessions expire after 10 minutes and are single-use; native CLI validates them. Exit code 0 or waiting logs do not prove login completion. On partial_success, authentication completed but the requested directory association was not verified: report this distinction, inspect account_info, and do not deploy or automatically retry creation. Reconfirm if the previous directory target changed. Never treat a workspace selection alone as permission to create, re-link or migrate; never read token caches or silently override credentials.
